scope: Seiko Alpinist 1959-2005 (vintage, revival and early-2000s compass-bezel models)
method_note: Tier 1 = Seiko-owned pages/manuals. HODINKEE Japan article is a Seiko-sponsored feature quoting collector Yoshihiko Honda (treated as third-party). The Spring Bar is a dealer blog (archived 2021) with some known errors (e.g. 1961 date). Unverified fields are null and listed in uncertain_fields.

compass_bezel_introduction.text: The internal rotating compass ring and the 4 o'clock crown that operates it first appear on the 1995 Alpinist (SCVF005/007/009). No 1959-1960s Alpinist had a compass.

history_facts.text: Seiko launches the Laurel Alpinist, its first sports watch, for mountaineering and skiing as both grew in popularity. It had a screw-back case against dust and sand, a leather watch pad against sweat, and luminous hands and indices.
Seiko says the large wedge-shaped indices at 3, 6, 9 and 12 gave high visibility day and night.
Seiko calls the Laurel Alpinist the starting point of its sports watches; its outdoor focus led to Japan's first diver's watch in 1965.
Sadao Ryugo's book dates the launch to December 1959 and calls it Seiko's first luminescent waterproof sports watch.
Launch price 4,500 yen per the 1959 SEIKO NEWS (standard Laurel 3,900 yen); cheaper than the contemporary Marvel and Cronos.
Champion Alpinist Type 1 (J13033), planned and designed by Daini Seikosha (Ryugo's book).
Champion Alpinist J13049 example dated 1962; snap caseback with the engraved Alpinist mountain logo.
Champion 850 Alpinist J13079 debuts in May 1963 with 24-hour markings unique to this reference (Ryugo's book).
Hodinkee Japan dates the Champion 850 Alpinist to about 1963, with a mountain motif on the caseback, and says Seiko named its sports models 'Alpinist' at the time.
Gold-plated and chrome-plated Champion 850 Alpinist (85899, cal. 851) reported from about 1964.
The Alpinist name drops out around the mid-1960s (about 1965 per Worn & Wound; 1964 per Time+Tide).
Seiko introduces the 4S movement family, which later powered the 1995 Alpinist. 1992 is the movement family's date, not the watch's.
The Alpinist name is revived with SCVF005/007/009 (cal. 4S15), designed by Shigeo Sakai. It adds the 4 o'clock crown, internal compass ring and date magnifier.
Designer Jun Tanaka (joined Seiko 1980) pushed for mechanical watches from about 1990, which led to the 1995 Alpinist revival (Ryugo's book).
The green SCVF009 colourway was inspired by Shigeo Sakai's almond-green Mini Cooper.
8F56 high-accuracy quartz Alpinists (SBCJ019/021/031) with GMT, perpetual calendar and compass ring join the line, plus the 500-piece SSASS limited edition SBCJ023.
Hodinkee Japan says Ikuhiro Kuzuya's 2006 redesign (SARB series, out of scope) replaced the 1995 design; green was used in both the 1995 and 2006 models.

models.name: Seiko Laurel Alpinist
models.production_period: 1959 (launched December 1959 per Sadao Ryugo) - c.1961; end date not documented

movement.notes: Signed 'Seikosha 17 jewels'; dial marked 'Diashock 17J'. No caliber number on the movement per Worn & Wound (for Champion Alpinist) and The Spring Bar. 18,000 vph per Fratello and The Spring Bar. Manufacturing factory (Suwa vs Daini Seikosha) for the Laurel Alpinist not confirmed by a primary source.

case.water_resistance: Screw-back 'dust-proof' case; Seiko describes it as highly airtight; Hodinkee Japan says it was called dust-proof (防塵) rather than water-resistant; no rating published
case.caseback: Screw-in stainless steel; engraved 'SEIKO LAUREL ALPINIST 14041 STAINLESS STEEL' (per The Spring Bar)
case.crown: Oversized crown, easy to wind (Fratello; Hodinkee Japan)

models.strap_bracelet: Leather strap with a large leather watch pad (cuff) to protect the watch from sweat (Seiko official). Third parties call it a bund-style strap.

msrp.source: 1959 SEIKO NEWS, as cited by HODINKEE Japan (Seiko-sponsored feature); standard Laurel was 3,900 JPY

design_notes: Seiko's first sports watch, per Seiko official pages.
Large wedge-shaped (mountain-shaped) luminous indices at 3, 6, 9 and 12; rectangular indices at the other hours (Seiko; Fratello).
Lume on all indices and on the hour and minute hands (Seiko official).
Dauphine/dagger-style hands; the seconds hand tip has a reddish colour (Fratello).
'Alpinist' script above 6 o'clock. The same logotype appears on later Alpinists (Fratello).
The only Alpinist to carry the Laurel name (Fratello).

Hodinkee Japan (quoting collector Yoshihiko Honda) says it grew out of the Suwa Seikosha Marvel Dust-Proof screw-back model and lumed Laurel variants. The Spring Bar notes Marvel and Champion watches using a 14041 case.

movements.notes: Diashock shock protection. No caliber number per W&W. Spring Bar says the Marvel had an almost identical movement. Factory (Suwa vs Daini) for each ref not confirmed by a primary source; Ryugo credits the Champion Alpinist design to Daini Seikosha.
Spring Bar reports 17J and 19J variants. Dealer sources say Seiko later moved to four-digit calibers (7622 lineage); not verified.

4S family introduced 1992. Derived from the 52xx family (grail-watch; Spring Bar cites 5246). 25.6mm diameter, 4.17mm height. Not chronometer-certified; Spring Bar's 'chronometer-grade' claim is unsupported.

movements.type: high-accuracy quartz, perpetual calendar, dual time (24-hour hand)

movements.notes: 196,608 Hz crystal; calendar to 28 Feb 2100; CR2412 battery, about 10 years; 4,800 A/m magnetic resistance; ultrasonic motor drives the calendar.
